📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 11:40 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 11:55 EST, 18 November 2026.

Those connected with Arsenal and England in particular, as well as Fulham, were in mourning on Tuesday following news of Peter Storey's death, aged 81.

The former right back and defensive midfielder died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family.

Arsenal confirmed that the club will pay their respects at their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund - which is their first home match post the international break - which takes place on November 24.

A club statement read: 'Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 double winner, Peter Storey.

'All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time. Rest in peace, Peter.'.

Storey enjoyed a stellar career at Arsenal, becoming a bona-fide legend in north London and earning a reputation as a tough tackler.

Arsenal legend Peter Storey died aged 81 on Tuesday in hospital after a short illness.

He played 501 games for Arsenal - placing him eighth on their all-time appearances list.

It has been revealed that joining the club as an apprentice in 1961, he made his first-team debut against Leicester City in October 1965. That outing was the first of 501 appearances for the club - a tally which places him eighth on their all-time list.

A tough tackler, Storey moved from right back to central midfield - playing a key role in their Fairs Cup triumph in 1970.

During the 1970-71 campaign, Storey was part of the Arsenal side which completed the double and played an notable part in their FA Cup success.

He scored a stoppage-time penalty against Stoke in the semi-finals to force a replay and the Gunners subsequently went on to lift the trophy.

Storey left the Gunners in 1977, scoring 19 goals across his time at the club, and moved to Fulham before retiring in 1978.

On the international stage, Storey was called up for England in 1971 and was capped 19 times - winning those between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey turned his hand to being a pub landlord. He owned a pub called the Jolly Farmers, now renamed De Beauvoir Arms, which was situated just over a mile away from Highbury - Arsenal's former home.

However, as his own autobiography - True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man - later details, Storey - who was married four times - was a 'confirmed ladies' man who loved a drink' and his establishment 'became a magnet for north London villains'.

Storey, who played at right back and in midfield, won 19 caps for England between 1971-1973.

Post-retirement, Storey got on the wrong side of the law multiple times for various offences.

Becoming acquaintances with criminals 'the Barry brothers' ended up seeing Storey serve time in prison as a result.

Storey aided the siblings' counterfeit operation by providing the finance and storage of the cast die for them to do so.

The trio were eventually caught and arrested - with Storey serving three years in prison at Wandsworth and Spring Hill for his actions.

However, the story does not end there. Far from it.

While on bail for conspiracy to produce counterfeit money, Storey looked to raise quick capital to flee to Spain.

Storey sought to do so by starting a brothel.

In a recent development, called the Calypso Massage Parlour, he set it up with three associates. That operation was short-lived though as he was arrested in December 1979, handed a £700 fine and given a six-month suspended sentence.

There were other run-ins with the law too. He was also briefly jailed for contempt of court after failing to appear at his bankruptcy hearings.

After his run-ins with the law, Storey moved to the south of France later in life (pictured in 2010).

In April 1982, he was given a 12-month suspended sentence for stealing two cars he had on hire purchase whilst running his minicab firm.

Eight years later, he spent 28 days in jail for attempting to import porn videos from Europe. However, he was caught when the videos were found in a spare tyre smuggled into the UK.

Storey, who later in life moved to the south of France, sold the majority of memorabilia for £20,000 years ago. However, he leaves behind plenty of memories as a player and post-retirement.

Una serata da dimenticare per Mauricio Pochettino, il cui debutto sulla panchina del Manchester United si trasforma in un autentico incubo. Ad Anfield, il Liverpool travolge i Red Devils con un netto 4-0 nell'undicesima giornata di Premier League. La partita prende subito una direzione precisa: all'8' Leny Yoro viene espulso per un fallo da ultimo uomo su Isak, lasciando gli ospiti in inferiorità numerica. Sulla conseguente punizione, Dominik Szoboszlai sblocca il risultato al 10' con una conclusione potente e rasoterra. Appena tre minuti dopo arriva il raddoppio di Florian Wirtz, che finalizza una splendida azione costruita da Ngumoha e Isak. Lo United prova a reagire con Fernandes e Tielemans, ma il Liverpool mantiene il controllo della gara.

Sources indicate that nella ripresa i Reds continuano ad attaccare, trovando sulla propria strada un ottimo Lammens, decisivo in diverse occasioni su Szoboszlai, Isak e Barcola. Al 66' arriva comunque il tris: Rio Ngumoha sfrutta l'assist di Barcola e firma il suo secondo gol stagionale in Premier League. All'81' Victor Munoz completa il poker, rendendo ancora più pesante la sconfitta dello United. Grazie a questo successo, il Liverpool sale al quarto posto con 21 punti, superando il Bournemouth e portandosi a una sola lunghezza dal Manchester City. Situazione sempre più delicata per i Red Devils, che restano penultimi con appena 8 punti, uno in più del Crystal Palace fanalino di coda. Per Pochettino, subentrato a Michael Carrick durante la sosta, l'avventura sulla panchina dello United comincia nel peggiore dei modi.

In a recent development, la Juventus si muoverà per una prima punta a gennaio. Dopo le trattative che vi abbiamo raccontato nei giorni scorsi, anche Luciano Spalletti si è esposto, dopo il successo sul Venezia: “Noi abbiamo bisogno di un giocatore lì perché non l'abbiamo comprato”, ha detto l’allenatore toscano tornando sulla campagna acquisti estiva.

L’analisi di Spalletti è poi proseguita: “Nel calcio d'oggi serve una punta fisica che sappia giocare spalle alla porta. Poi è inutile parlare di Spalletti via. C'è bisogno di gente fisica, che riceva la pallata addosso e sappia giocare con le mani addosso del centrale avversario. Ora è così. Si vince i duelli. Ci vuole gente fisica che vinca i duelli ed esca dalle mini prigioni che ci sono in campo”. Una richiesta chiara, con la società che già da qualche settimana ha attivato i contatti in questo senso.

Chi sono i nomi seguiti dalla Juventus? Uno è sempre quell’Alexander Sorloth dell’Atletico Madrid a lungo cercato in estate. In questo avvio di stagione con Simeone non sta trovando spazio, possibile che fra qualche settimana possa diventare un’occasione. Altro nome forte è Falorin Balogun, che il Monaco non svenderò nonostante una scarsa centralità nel progetto. In Italia potrebbero tornare a scaldarsi i nomi di Antonio Raimondo e Gianluca Scamacca, ma è soprattutto Gustavo Varela a stuzzicare le idee bianconere. Anche se per il suo cartellino serviranno fra i 30 ed i 40 milioni di euro.

L’incrocio sarebbe avvenuto sabato 21 novembre, mentre i due gruppi viaggiavano verso Parma e Napoli.

Gruppi di tifosi della Roma e del Torino sarebbero entrati in contatto sull’Autostrada del Sole durante le trasferte di sabato 21 novembre. Secondo le prime ricostruzioni riportate da la Repubblica, alcuni van dei granata sono stati danneggiati. Si parla anche di feriti.

Le due tifoserie si sarebbero incrociate sull’A1. Il contatto tra i gruppi sarebbe poi degenerato in violenza.

I sostenitori erano in viaggio verso Parma e Napoli per seguire le rispettive squadre.

Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman.
  • "The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful!
  • Industry observers note that at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is an obligation on all of us, from supporters to pundits and journalists, to remain calm and measured about footballers as young as Max Dowman. But, my word, he does make it difficult. Arsenal’s 16-year-old sensation continues to sparkle whenever he steps on to the field, and he did so again with this superb display against Ipswich Town.

"The hype will only continue to grow!"Max Dowman that is delightful! 👏 pic.twitter.com/UfFY1VSyXn.

Industry observers note that at this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Sources indicate that dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

It has been revealed that max Dowman nets his second of the game! 😍 pic.twitter.com/XRZ9GqZx3x.

Recent findings suggest that as Mikel Arteta approaches the point of signing a fresh contract in north London, one wonders how much the idea of developing Dowman will excite him as he looks to the future. Which manager would not want to coach a player of such natural ability? Which manager would not want to see how good he could be? The same is true of Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who also impressed on Tuesday night.

“A joy to have him,” said Arteta of Dowman. “It’s remarkable. It’s something very natural for him. He can deliver those actions effortlessly, I would say. What we have to do is look after him. He is 16. You don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context.

Industry observers note that “Having two teenagers playing for Arsenal at this level is so fulfilling. Because I’ve been there and just to be able to contribute to somebody’s career and dream, to be able to experience a game like tonight, is phenomenal. And yeah, medium and long term, we know that if they continue to develop in the way that they are, we are going to have two tremendous footballers.”.

"He was brilliant, he made the difference - we need to look after him" 🌟Mikel Arteta says Arsenal need to "be really cautious" with 16-year-old Max Dowman after he scored twice in Arsenal's 4-2 win over Ipswich 🔴 pic.twitter.com/1msJAEkK8z.

Sources indicate that dowman’s two goals, along with strikes by Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino, secured a comfortable victory for Arsenal against Premier League opponents. Ipswich scored a goal of their own, through Anis Mehmeti, but never seemed likely to cause the visitors too much bother. A late strike from former Arsenal player Chuba Akpom was only a consolation. “We found a way to fight back into it,” said Gary O’Neil. “Losing by two goals to them isn’t a dreadful effort.”.

Dowman is already developing a trademark goal, of sorts. His first strike for the club, against Everton last season, came after he left an opponent face-down on the turf at the Emirates Stadium. He inflicted the same pain here upon poor Cédric Kipré, who tried to tackle the teenager in the seventh minute but ended up with a mouthful of grass.

Recent findings suggest that it was an image that encapsulated Arsenal’s dominance in the early exchanges, as was the sight of Madueke firing in the second. The chance came after Bruno Guimarães and Merino, majestic in midfield, had monstered Ipswich’s attempts to play out from the back. Merino was dominant throughout, winning tackles with steel and then spinning away opponents with style. “He’s unbelievable,” remarked Arteta.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal’s long-term relationship with the League Cup is not a particularly healthy one. For a club of their stature, it is a source of mild embarrassment that they have not won this competition since 1993. They came close last season, reaching the final at Wembley, but were defeated by Manchester City.

Given the depth of Arteta’s squad, Arsenal really should reach the final again. If this is a tournament for the B-team, at least in these early stages, then Arsenal probably have the best B-team in the country. They started this game without any of Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Martin Odegaard, and Kai Havertz but were still extraordinarily strong in midfield and attack.

The only pre-match concern was their defence, which has been weakened by a couple of early-season injuries. Arsenal started with Salmon at centre-back and the teenager was in direct combat with the physical, sharp-elbowed threat of Ipswich striker Zian Flemming. He stood up to the challenge with determination and class.

Ipswich had made 10 changes following their victory at Crystal Palace at the weekend, which was an indication of where the Carabao Cup sits in their priorities. They were able to get into Arsenal’s penalty area but never gave the impression they could really hurt the Premier League champions, apart from when Mehmeti converted Jack Clarke’s low cross.

Sources indicate that akpom struck in the 91st minute to encourage O’Neil, but by then the game had been lost. Arsenal’s work, and indeed Dowman’s work, had been done.

"He's 16 years old, and we have to be cautious of that" 💫Mikel Arteta reacts to an incredible performance from Max Dowman as Arsenal put FOUR past Ipswich 🔴Don't miss the Carabao Cup on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/AIcAbMx6ub.

Sources indicate that on managing the hype that surrounds Dowman, Arteta said: “What we have to do is look after him. He’s 16 years old, you don’t see that in this league. In other leagues in Europe, that’s a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands... We need to make sure that every time we throw him in it’s in the right context with the right preparation.”.

Conor Coady shares his thoughts on Arteta’s role in Dowman’s development:.

"He'll know how to nurture him!" 🗣️Conor Coady says Mikel Arteta is the perfect manager for Max Dowman 👏 pic.twitter.com/YdgLxfKiOf.

Asked about Dowman’s two-goal performance, Arteta said: “A joy to have him, Marli [Salmon] as well. Seventeen years old, to play at that level with the physicality they have to be able to handle that level, it’s remarkable. Max, yeah, it’s inevitable to talk about him when he scores and he creates the moments he has created tonight. It’s normal.”.

Industry observers note that he added: “He is coping better and better and better, he did the action where he regains the ball and wins it in the first goal, he loses his man... He’s an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play on the biggest stage and still handles the situation with such naturality.”.

According to recent reports, speaking in his post-match press conference, Mikel Arteta stated: “Really pleased with a lot of things we did tonight, the way we attacked the game, how dominant, fluid and aggressive we were, right from the beginning to try to influence the result. We scored two very early goals that gave us obviously a great platform for the game.

It has been revealed that “Individually some massive performances as well. Some debuts tonight which is great to see as well, so we take a lot of positives from tonight.”.

Arsenal have won the League Cup twice – in 1987 and 1993 – meaning eight clubs have better records, including Aston Villa (five titles), Tottenham Hotspur (four), Nottingham Forest (four) and Leicester City (three).

Recent findings suggest that their rather modest haul is a far cry from their record-setting 14 FA Cup titles. In the 33-years since Arsenal’s most recent League Cup triumph, the competition’s title sponsor has changed hands four times (kudos to anyone who can name all five!).

No team has scored more goals through substitutes in the Premier League than Ipswich, which is a nod to the promoted club’s depth and work in the summer transfer window.

It has meant that Gary O’Neil has had to leave established players out of match-day squads. “It was really tough leaving out Darnell [Furlong] and Anis [Mehmeti] from the squad [against Crystal Palace],” he said. “Doing that to good people is one of the toughest parts of the job. But I have faith in them, it’s just that everyone’s fit at the moment and we’ve had to recruit a strong squad to get us through an unbelievably challenging season.

“On Tuesday, whoever I pick, I have 100 per cent faith that they’re ready and that they’re going to represent what we do and how we go about it.”.

On Hincapie’s omission from the match-day squad:.

“Some players were carrying some fatigue, some little issues that we have to look after and some other players are available, fresh and in better conditions to play.

On Timber being left out of tonight’s squad:.

According to recent reports, “Everything is fine, but obviously he has played much more than we would have wanted. He played 53 minutes [against Sunderland] after five months. I will need to look after him.”.

When asked if Arsenal will set up with a back three tonight:.

Recent findings suggest that alan Davies, the actor and comedian who is a famously passionate supporter of Arsenal, recently told a story about a charity event he once attended with former captain Tony Adams. Speaking on The Tuesday Club podcast, Davies stated Adams revealed his football philosophy to be: “You need seven.”.

Sources indicate that the “seven” in question, Adams explained, are seven members of the team who are ready and willing to fight the opposition in the tunnel after the game. Once a team have those seven individuals, Adams said, everything else flows from there.

For much of the past two decades, Arsenal have not had seven. In some years in the latter stages of Arsène Wenger’s tenure, they probably did not even have three or four. But that has all changed in recent seasons under Mikel Arteta, to such an extent that the Premier League champions would now undoubtedly bring considerably more than seven combatants to any touchline scrap or tunnel bust-up.

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

Newcastle chiefs have held a secret meeting with the money men of Wall Street after advanced talks with Goldman Sachs over the financing of a newly introduced £1.3billion super stadium – the strongest indication yet that the club are preparing to leave St James' Park.

I can reveal senior representatives from the American investment banking giant were on Tyneside this month, with sources claiming the trip was aimed at 'finalising' the proposed funding structure for a spectacular new 65,000-seater home on Leazes Park.

Interestingly, the meeting came in a week when Jacobo Solis, the influential Public Investment Fund executive and club director who is rarely seen in the city, was also present. The Spaniard’s involvement is viewed as extremely significant by those close to the project, and we understand an announcement on the club’s stadium aims is now ‘very close’.

The high-level meeting with Goldman Sachs is a major indication the club's board will recommend the development of a new stadium rather than redeveloping St James’, and I understand the former is right now the preference.

Recent findings suggest that there has been significant outlay on various surveys around Leazes Park in recent months. I reported in April how the presence of bats in the area was one environmental complication they had to overcome. The club has since undertaken extensive work around animal and plant life.

The alternative remains a St James’ expansion, taking the capacity to 60,000, but chief executive David Hopkinson and others among the top brass are well aware that only a fresh, multi-purpose home would allow Newcastle to compete financially with the world’s biggest clubs.

A secret meeting with representatives from Goldman Sachs is the strongest indication yet the club are preparing to leave St James' Park rather than redevelop it.

In April, Daily Mail Sport revealed an architect’s drawing of how the latest, three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated.

Plans of the new stadium reveal an exterior that has been likened to Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena.

Sources indicate that the proposed funding model combines borrowing, owner investment and potentially outside investors, with the debt sitting with Newcastle rather than the ownership. That makes the involvement of Goldman Sachs particularly significant as the club look to turn their ambitious plans into a financially viable reality.

Sources have described the circular design of a new stadium, and in April we revealed an architect’s drawing of how the three-tier venue would look. Those drawings, by architects at KSS, have since been updated, but the exterior has been likened to both Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena and Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium by those who have seen images and video.

In a recent development, club sources say they are continuing to work on options and plans for a new stadium. But the visit of Goldman Sachs – and the simultaneous presence of one of PIF's most influential figures – suggests that work behind the scenes is moving towards a decisive stage.

Having covered this story for several years, I now believe PIF will be asked to sign off on a latest stadium development ahead of an announcement in early 2027.

Dedic case closed - but he's told to bow out.

Amar Dedic has been given a rap on the knuckles and handed over his bow and arrows after the Newcastle defender’s ‘suspicious activity’ triggered a major police operation earlier this month.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed on November 5 that the Bosnian was at the centre of a search involving at least six patrol cars after he was spotted carrying the hunting weaponry at a Northumberland beauty spot.

A concerned 999 caller, believing there could be a threat to the public, reported seeing him and a friend walking with the equipment near a reservoir in the countryside outside Newcastle.

Police dispatched marked and unmarked vehicles to the Harlow Hill area, with some understood to have been armed response units, before Dedic and his companion were intercepted in a blaze of blue lights around seven miles away in the exclusive Darras Hall estate.

Newcastle United's Amar Dedic has had his bow and arrows taken away from him after causing a major incident earlier this month.

It has been revealed that in a bizarre twist, Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie and former defender Paul Dummett arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic and his friend. After lengthy discussions at the roadside, police were satisfied that Dedic was using the weaponry for recreational use, but their investigation remained open.

However, I can confirm the matter is now closed and the 24-year-old has been reminded of UK law by police and the club. Hunting any animal or bird with a bow and arrow or crossbow is illegal in this country.

A Northumbria Police spokesperson told me: ‘Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, November 4, we received a report of suspicious activity in the Harlow Hill area.

Sources indicate that ‘It was reported that two men had been witnessed in possession of bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road. Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows.

According to recent reports, 'At that time, it was understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public. Following a number of enquiries, this has now been confirmed. The two men have since forfeited the bow and arrows and words of advice have been given to the pair. The case has now been closed.’.

Dedic took the confusion in good spirit, posting a picture of Lord of the Rings character Legolas, known for his prowess with a bow and arrow, on his social media page.

Joelinton has not yet been ruled out of the Tyne-Wear derby, despite fears over a significant injury lay-off.

I revealed on November 4 that the Brazilian had suffered a fresh muscle strain and this was confirmed by Matthias Jaissle the following day. There has been a suggestion this week that the period out could extend towards Christmas, but sources have played down that possibility.

I understand Joelinton is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures. This could still be too soon for the visit of Sunderland on December 6, but the noises around the midfielder have definitely been more optimistic in the past 24 hours. The 30-year-old is expected to be the only senior absentee from the squad that takes on Arsenal this weekend.

Joelinton (left) is expected to be back in action long before the festive fixtures.

Sources indicate that newcastle will NOT be signing Gambian triallists Omar Marong and Alieu Saine. I understand that, while the 16-year-olds have impressed during a two-week stay, club chiefs have decided that those already on the books are of greater potential.

It has been revealed that marong and Saine played in a 6-0 win over the i2i International Soccer Academy on Friday, and winger Saine chipped in with two assists. However, while there is a feeling both will secure moves to Europe in due course, Newcastle will keep a watching brief for now.

The pair are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and were identified by the club’s newly introduced global talent team. They caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals.

Neither player could have signed permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle were keen to assess their potential. It is likely that players of a similar profile from Africa will arrive on trial in the future.

Arteta to meet old foe at St James'.

Recent findings suggest that both Jaissle and Mikel Arteta will walk suspension tightropes at St James’ Park on Saturday. The Newcastle and Arsenal bosses are on two bookings for the season – and a third means a one-game touchline ban.

Interestingly, the fourth official with whom Arteta clashed at Sunderland earlier this season will be on duty. Elliot Bell repeatedly warned Arteta not to step from his technical zone at the Stadium of Light.

Industry observers note that when the Spaniard infringed on Sunderland’s managerial area for a third time, referee John Brooks issued a yellow card. Arteta then appeared to sarcastically target Bell with a ‘just tick the box’ gesture.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle is a booking away from a one-game touchline ban.

The 2023 match between Newcastle and Arsenal at St James' Park was settled by a controversial winner, with Joelinton accused of a push on Gabriel.

In another twist, Stuart Attwell will be the VAR this weekend. He was the referee in charge when Newcastle beat Arsenal 1-0 three years ago. The controversial winning goal that night was scored by Anthony Gordon amid suspicion the ball had run out of play before Joe Willock crossed.

Joelinton was then accused by Arsenal of a push on defender Gabriel, while Gordon looked offside. All three incidents survived VAR checks and Attwell’s on-field decision stood.

Arteta was furious and branded the decision an ‘absolute disgrace’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arsenal subsequently issued an official statement backing his criticism and demanded improved refereeing standards. Arteta was charged by the FA over his comments but was eventually cleared.

However, the Premier League's independent Key Match Incidents panel ruled by a 4-1 majority that the goal had correctly been allowed to stand.

Finally, after James Trafford starred during England's 3-2 win in Spain this week, a brilliant match I was lucky enough to cover, one reader reached out to ask about an XI of players Newcastle have missed out on.

The club tried to sign Trafford on three occasions under Eddie Howe, and even as recently as this summer he appeared destined for Tyneside.

So, with thanks to the idea from Ian Spencer, here is the ‘what might have been’ XI of Newcastle targets who came close to signing….

Newcastle's What Might Have Been XI (3-5-2): James Trafford; Abdukodir Khusanov, Tosin Adarabioyo, Marc Guehi; Ivan Fresneda, Johan Manzambi, Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg, James Maddison, Victor Munoz; Joao Pedro, Hugo Ekitike.

Would this XI beat the current side? Answers in the comments below please!

Nunziante 6 - Subisce il Goal di Artistico su cui non poteva fare niente, ma si è fatto trovare sempre attento nelle varie conclusioni avversarie.

Renzi 6 -Nonostante l’ammonizione ha disputato una grande gara in fase difensiva annullando Di Mariano e difendendo bene anche su altri giocatori.

Gilli 5.5 - E’ sempre stato ordinato dando sicurezza al reparto, ha peccato però sul goal avversario con una piccola distrazione.

Illanes 5.5 - Stessa valutazione di Gilli, ha disputato una buona partita ma ha peccato di distrazione sul goal subito.

Cagnano 6 - Anche lui ha difeso bene sulla sua fascia di competenza dimostrandosi un difensore rognoso, pecca per lui l’ammonizione subita Dal 46’ Righetti 6 -Anche per lui una buona partita, ha tenuto bene la posizione non facendosi sorprendere sugli attacchi avversari.

Mawuli 6 - Ad inizio partita si è visto poco, ma con il passare dei minuti si è dimostrato più intraprendente prendendo in mano le chiavi del centrocampo toscano Dal 61’ Iaccarino 6 - Ha cercato di dare equilibrio in mezzo al campo senza però trovare la giocata giusta.

Arena 6 - Buona partita per lui, ha dato un gran supporto in fase offensiva spingendo con costanza ed arrivando più volte a cross e tiri pericolosi Dal 61’ Pattarella 6.5 - Grande impatto sulla partita per lui, creando molte occasioni offensive di cui alcune pericolose.

Sala 6.5 - Ha corso molto ed è sempre stato nel vivo del gioco dimostrandosi una pedina importante per Bucchi.

Ionita 5.5 - Non cattura l’occhio degli spettatori ed è troppo passivo in fase difensiva, ma a centrocampo riesce ad alzare abbastanza la qualità del gioco e l’indice di pericolosità dei suoi.

Tavernelli 6.5 - Ha dato il suo contributo offensivo con l’assist e mostrandosi fastidioso per la difesa avversaria.

Mancuso 7 - E’ l’autore del momentaneo vantaggio amaranto, nel resto della partita è stato utile alla squadra nei ripiegamenti e dando sempre una linea di passaggio ai compagni Dal 82’Cerri - s.v.

Sorrentino 6 - Non è stato chiamato in causa più di tanto, ma ha saputo rispondere in maniera positiva alle conclusioni avversarie: sul goal subito non avrebbe potuto fare più di tanto.

Allenatore: Calabro 6 - La sua squadra ha gestito di più il gioco ma non è mai riuscita ad essere veramente pericolosa.

La domenica di Serie A propone una sfida importante alla New Balance Arena di Bergamo, dove l'Atalanta ospita l'Inter. Le due formazioni arrivano all'appuntamento del 22 novembre attraversando momenti decisamente differenti: la squadra di Cristian Chivu occupa il terzo posto in classifica (scavalcata dalla Roma ieri) e vuole proseguire la propria corsa nelle zone altissime, mentre quella di Maurizio Sarri è scivolata fino alla dodicesima posizione, pagando una serie di risultati poco convincenti.

Il momento della Dea è particolarmente delicato: nelle ultime cinque partite tra tutte le competizioni è arrivata una sola vittoria, con la pesante sconfitta casalinga per 3-0 contro il Parma e i pareggi consecutivi contro Frosinone e Fiorentina. Decisamente migliore il rendimento recente dell'Inter, capace di conquistare quattro successi nelle ultime cinque gare. Tra questi spiccano il 3-0 rifilato al Feyenoord in Champions League e il 2-0 contro il Como prima della sosta per le nazionali. L'unico passo falso dei nerazzurri milanesi è stato il derby perso 3-1 contro il Milan. A Bergamo, dunque, si affrontano due squadre con esigenze differenti: l'Inter vuole consolidare la propria posizione di vertice, mentre l'Atalanta cerca una vittoria per invertire la rotta. Di seguito le formazioni ufficiali.

According to recent reports, atalanta (4-2-3-1): Carnesecchi; Bellanova, Scalvini, Kolasinac, Zappacosta; Kessié, Ederson; Elmas, De Ketelaere, Zalewski; Krstovic. Allenatore: Maurizio Sarri Inter (3-5-2): Martinez J.; Pavard, Bastoni, Carlos Augusto; Spence, Barella, Calhanoglu, Mkhitaryan, Dimarco; Esposito, Thuram. Allenatore: Cristian Chivu.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

One source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are said to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

It has been revealed that italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

Van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which demonstrates his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their new deals.

In a recent development, alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing matter for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

It was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

Well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

In a recent development, slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

In a recent development, he is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

It has been revealed that the Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

According to recent reports, confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

In the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

In the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

According to recent reports, since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Substantial Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a new-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

It has been revealed that liverpool need to see more from their big-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

Spurs finally score... but still lose

📅 16 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.
  • Sources indicate that it could have been something different.
  • Sources indicate that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

Sources indicate that it could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, demonstrated this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

Sources indicate that “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

Industry observers note that THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

“We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

Sources indicate that rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

Significant save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

Industry observers note that the miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that for all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

Industry observers note that “I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he demonstrates is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Sources indicate that simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

Industry observers note that pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

According to recent reports, is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he indicated two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

It has been revealed that his mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

His touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Recent findings suggest that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

It has been revealed that from that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

According to recent reports, spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo remarked.

In a recent development, he was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

Double change for Tottenham as Savio and Maddison replace Kudus and Gallagher.

Change for Liverpool as Barcola replaces Ngumoha.

Double change for Liverpool as Szoboszlai and Gravenberch replace Nyoni and McConnell in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield.

Recent findings suggest that mac Allister takes but his effort is off target. That is indeed the final moment of the half and Liverpool take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of that fine Mac Allister strike.

Sources indicate that we are past the two initial minutes added on but that is because of the delay when Senesi was given a talking-to moments ago. That allows Liverpool to win a free-kick not far outside the Tottenham box and Bentancur is booked for the foul on Gakpo.

Recent findings suggest that that is a dreadful decision from referee Andy Madley. Frimpong gets the better of Tel in a contest down Tottenham’s left, with the former outmuscling the latter. Not only is Frimpong penalised, he is booked.

Sources indicate that mac Allister spurns a glorious chance to get his and Liverpool’s second of the night. Tottenham again risk it at the back and lose it. McConnell then feeds a pass into the box to pick out the run of Koumas, who squares it for Mac Allister. The Argentine cannot get his feet sorted in time and wastes the opportunity from eight yards out.

Liverpool want a penalty. Tottenham give it away cheaply inside their own box and McConnell goes down under a challenge from Senesi, who was the one who gave it away. It was a clumsy challenge from Senesi and if VAR was in action tonight it would have been interesting to see what they would have done with that as Senesi did barge into the back of McConnell.

Araujo is then booked for pulling Marmoush back.

Sources indicate that there is no way Tottenham’s goal drought will last in perpetuity but they have missed two fabulous chances so far and you wonder what impact that will have on their confidence. At least one Tottenham player is being feted: Andy Robertson, who has just jogged down the touchline at Anfield in a different kit for the first time in nine years. He tried not to acknowledge the singing of his name too much but you could see it meant something to him.

The home fans serenade their former player Robertson as the now Tottenham left-back goes out to warm up.

According to recent reports, that is a substantial chance for Kudus to equalise on the counter. Tottenham break from deep inside their own half and charge down their left. Bergvall waits for Udogie to come on the overlap before playing the pass. From the left side of the box, Udogie crosses for Kudus, who gets across the front of Kerkez. Kudus should probably score but lifts his effort over the bar from just six yards out.

That was a chance for Udogie. Senesi clips in a lovely ball over the top in behind to pick out the run from left-back of Udogie, who tries to chest it down but cannot keep it under control. Had he done so, it would have been a great chance.

According to recent reports, the way Alexis Mac Allister has played this past fortnight, anyone would think he is trying to secure himself a newly introduced contract. All cynicism aside, that was a quite beautiful goal and attention must be drawn to Cody Gakpo’s involvement: he took a pass on his chest from Joe Gomez before opening up the pitch. We will say it again: the idea of selling Gakpo in the last window was madness.

He scored a stunner nearly a week ago against Atletico Madrid here in the Champions League and he adds another storming strike to his repertoire. The ball finds kindly to Mac Allister on the edge of the box after Udogie tackled Ngumoha and the Argentine finds the top corner with a first-time finish.

Ngumoha slides a clinical pass into the box to pick out the run in behind of Koumas, who gets the better of Senesi. Koumas takes a great first touch before getting his shot away but is denied by Dubravka. Both goalkeepers have now been forced into good saves early doors.

The heavens have well and truly opened at Anfield, with the rain heaving down.

Tottenham win a corner off Gomez out on the right. Kudus clips in an inswinger that Araujo heads away.

Gakpo is starting out on the left for Liverpool tonight, with Ngumoha on the right and Koumas leading the line down the centre. Gakpo was linked with a move to Tottenham and Manchester City over the summer but stayed at Liverpool.

Tottenham have a free-kick not far outside the Liverpool penalty area on the right as Kerkez is penalised for blocking Gallagher’s cross with his arm. Kudus’ delivery is headed away by Araujo.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

It is understood that De Zerbi’s lucrative contract did not include a survival bonus for avoiding relegation last season, but he must wish his forwards were cashing in on their goal bonuses.

Our team to take on Tottenham Hotspur 🔴 pic.twitter.com/tZSJkPpH3y.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

In a recent development, “I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

Industry observers note that “But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no challenges. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

Sources indicate that liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Industry observers note that tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

Recent findings suggest that “I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi stated. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have major confidence in my players, they are very good players.

Recent findings suggest that “We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I mentioned we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

Sources indicate that tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

Una lunga intervista quella che il Ct della Nazionale Femminile Andrea Soncin ha rilasciato a Sportweek, il settimanale in edicola ogni sabato con La Gazzetta dello Sport, dove sono stati toccati tantissimi tempi, non solo inerenti al campo: il tecnico ha infatti insistito molto anche sullo sviluppo del momento femminile in Italia.

Ma appunto, come detto, si è parlato anche di campo, e questo è stato il suo commento: "Dobbiamo provare ad alzare sempre di più il livello del prodotto, anche nella creazione di infrastrutture che possano rendere lo spettacolo più coinvolgente. Sappiamo bene che i nostri risultati possono accendere ancora di più i fari su tutto il movimento, però poi servono visione e progettualità. E ora vogliamo portare tutti al Mondiale. E nei sogni di tutte noi andare a giocare questo torneo in un paese iconico come il Brasile".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

40′ – Attacca la Lazio, tiro forte e teso di Mazzei, Mataluna respinge.

37′ – Tambaro serve Cacciapuoti che entra in area da sinistra, calcia verso la porta, ma Folgori c’è e blocca.

37′ – Triplo cambio nel Napoli: fuori Iavarone, Roma e Maglio; dentro Federico, Gallo e Ryzhak.

32′ – Cambio nel Napoli: fuori Schettino, dentro Giliberti.

31′ – Ammonito il tecnico del Napoli Liguori per proteste.

24′ – Cambi nella Lazio: fuori Vender e Spoletini; dentro Sciarpelletti e Costantino.

21′ – Cambio nel Napoli: fuori Ciotola, dentro Di Domenico.

20′ – Sugli sviluppi del corner, colpo di testa di Massa che finisce di poco a lato.

20′ – Cross profondo di Tambaro sul secondo palo, deviazione pericolosa della Lazio, palla che finisce in corner.

14′ – Maglio recupera palla dal limite dell’area su un retropassaggio sbagliato della Lazio. Entra in area, calcia ma Folgori devia e la difesa allontana.

9′ – Cambio nella Lazio: esce Kone ed entra Piras.

3′ – Chirico perde il possesso della palla, Kone parte in contropiede verso l’area di rigore, uscita di Mataluna che è bravo a respingere il suo tiro.

14:30 – Inizia la ripresa, batte la Lazio.

39′ – Occasione Napoli allo scadere: cross dalla sinistra, sul secondo palo arriva Maglio in corsa, ma era molto defilato, il suo pallonetto finisce alto.

22′ – Occasione per il Napoli: cross basso dalla destra, e dopo un rimpallo, Ciotola calcia di prima intenzione, il suo tiro finisce alto.

17′ – Ammonito il tecnico della Lazio Gualdaroni per proteste.

16′ – Doppia occasione per la Lazio: cross dalla destra, Spoletini colpisce di testa, ma respinge Mataluna. Sulla ribattuta ancora Spoletini ci prova, ma Mataluna mette in corner.

4′ – Contropiede del Napoli: Tambaro porta via il pallone centralmente, poi scarica a Ciotola in area, che calcia a botta sicura, la Lazio salva sulla linea.

3′ – Ripartenza dal basso sbagliata della Lazio, Maglio recupera palla dal limite ma calcia sul fondo.

13:35 – Inizia il match, batte il Napoli.

Napoli: 1 Mataluna, 2 Iavarone, 3 Ferrara, 4 Massa, 5 Chirico, 6 Roma, 7 Maglio, 8 Ciotola, 9 Schettino, 10 Tambaro (C), 11 Cacciapuoti. A disp. 12 Cuomo, 13 Federico, 14 Gallo, 15 Palmelli, 16 Di Domenico, 17 Pietropinto, 18 Giliberti, 19 Michieli, 20 Ryzhak . All. Liguori.

Lazio: 1 Folgori, 2 Rufo, 3 Mazzei, 4 Zauri, 5 Toci, 6 Vender, 7 Licciardello, 8 Mancini (C), 9 Kone, 10 Spoletini, 11 Vinci. A disp. 12 Jiboc, 13 Coccia, 14 Giampaolo, 15 Monforte, 16 Sciarpelletti, 17 Costantino, 18 Carlopio, 19 Scorzafave, 20 Piras. All. Gualdaroni.

Benvenuti alla diretta testuale di IamNaples.it di Napoli-Lazio, gara valida per la decima giornata del campionato Under 15 girone C. Gli azzurrini sono primi in classifica con 24 punti, hanno vinto otto gare su nove cadendo solo sul campo della Fiorentina e sono reduci dal successo in trasferta contro l’Arezzo. La Lazio è seconda insieme alla Fiorentina a quattro lunghezze dagli azzurrini, lo scorso weekend ha vinto 1-0 il derby contro la Roma.

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 14:09 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EST, 18 November 2026.

Leicester have decided to end their deal with controversial sponsors BC.GAME six months ahead of schedule.

Fans expressed fury and dismay earlier this month after the club's unlicensed gambling shirt sponsor appointed an 'international porn star' as its new ambassador.

It has been revealed that now Leicester have opted to conclude the partnership – in a move welcomed by supporters. A statement on Wednesday read: ‘The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

‘We would like to thank BC.GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

‘Supporters who have purchased a BC.GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December.’.

BC.GAME, an online casino company, had been the Foxes' primary shirt sponsor since the start of the 2024-25 season. They declared a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie in a video on X earlier this month.

Leicester City have axed a partnership with BC.GAME, after the gambling shirt sponsor appointed 'international porn star' Eva Elfie as its latest ambassador.

Leicester confirmed fans who have purchased a replica shirt featuring the sponsor's name within the last 28 days can return it for a full refund or exchange by December 2.

Elfie, who has 4.8million Instagram followers, is known in Esports and gaming communities too.

In recent years, Leicester’s spectacular decline on the pitch has mirrored the relationship with their supporters.

During the years immediately before and after their stunning Premier League triumph in 2016, it was difficult to find a club more in tune with the fanbase.

But a series of baffling decisions – including the tie-up with BC.GAME – eroded trust between the club and their supporters.

Leicester are now in League One and face a long road back but sensible moves like this one suggest they are at least facing in the right direction again.

Velocità e cinismo, il Milan travolge il Frosinone: 5-1 a San Siro con un super Rabiot

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (315 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that il Milan supera con un netto 5-1 il Frosinone al termine di una partita rimasta in equilibrio fino al 3-1.
  • Recent findings suggest that L'avvio sorride ai ciociari, aggressivi fin dai primi secondi e subito vicini al vantaggio con la traversa colpita da Masini.
  • It has been revealed that L'inizio della ripresa indirizza definitivamente la sfida.

Recent findings suggest that il Milan supera con un netto 5-1 il Frosinone al termine di una partita rimasta in equilibrio fino al 3-1. A sbloccarla è lo sfortunato autogol di Calvani, seguito dall'attesa rete di Gonçalo Ramos. Masini riapre i giochi prima della mezzora, ma nella ripresa Jashari, Cissé e Pulisic chiudono definitivamente i conti. La squadra di Amorim interpreta la gara alla perfezione, rispettando un avversario coraggioso ma sfruttando con qualità e velocità ogni spazio concesso. La vittoria è netta ed è la sesta nelle ultime sette partite di campionato per il Diavolo.

Recent findings suggest that L'avvio sorride ai ciociari, aggressivi fin dai primi secondi e subito vicini al vantaggio con la traversa colpita da Masini. Il pressing alto mette inizialmente in difficoltà il Milan, che però dimostra grande maturità tattica: invece di forzare le giocate, aspetta il momento giusto per uscire dalla pressione. Così arriva il vantaggio con l'autogol di Calvani, mentre il raddoppio nasce da una ripartenza perfetta finalizzata da Ramos dopo un'azione corale. Protagonista in entrambe le occasioni Rabiot, altruista e vero uomo squadra. Il Frosinone, comunque, non rinuncia ad attaccare e trova il meritato 2-1 con Masini, mantenendo aperta una gara intensa e spettacolare fino all'intervallo.

It has been revealed that L'inizio della ripresa indirizza definitivamente la sfida. Moreira sfiora subito il tris, poi Jashari (subentrato a Bartesaghi) firma il 3-1 con una conclusione imprendibile sotto la traversa. Il Frosinone prova ancora a reagire e costruisce occasioni importanti, ma non riesce a riaprire l'incontro. Da quel momento il Milan diventa dominante: ogni recupero si trasforma in una potenziale ripartenza letale. Cissé, appena entrato, cala il poker dopo l'intervento del VAR, mentre un grave errore dei padroni di casa spalanca a Pulisic la strada per il definitivo 5-1. Nel finale Moreira sfiora anche il sesto gol, a conferma di una prestazione quasi perfetta dei rossoneri.

Il caso Jamal Musiala continua ad agitare il Bayern Monaco e adesso coinvolge anche Michael Olise. L'esterno francese ha messo “mi piace” su Instagram a un post di Fabrizio Romano che riportava la presa di posizione della FIFPRO, il sindacato internazionale dei calciatori, in difesa del centrocampista tedesco: “Il Bayern deve rispettare Musiala”. Un gesto che potrebbe rappresentare un segnale di disapprovazione nei confronti della dirigenza bavarese, finita al centro delle polemiche per alcune dichiarazioni pubbliche sulle condizioni e sul futuro del giocatore.

According to recent reports, nelle ultime settimane Uli Hoeness, Jan-Christian Dreesen e Karl-Heinz Rummenigge hanno espresso dubbi sulle possibilità di recupero del ventitreenne, alle prese con una disfunzione neurologica che provoca brevi crisi epilettiche. Particolarmente pesanti le parole di Rummenigge a Sky: “Quello che sappiamo, purtroppo, suggerisce che sarà difficile per lui tornare al livello che ha dimostrato così spesso qui in questo stadio”. Secondo la Bild, la ricerca della terapia farmacologica più adatta resta complessa. Sullo sfondo anche la questione economica: Musiala percepirebbe circa 25 milioni di euro annui e il Bayern starebbe valutando un adeguamento dell'ingaggio in relazione al rendimento sportivo.

A mettere in guardia il club è stato Maik Franz, ex vicepresidente dell'associazione calciatori tedesca VDV, intervenuto a Sport1: “Con Michael Olise, potreste avere tra le vostre fila il secondo miglior calciatore del mondo. Volete che rinnovi il contratto e che guadagni uno stipendio elevato. Ma, in fondo, penserà: 'Se mi ammalo o mi infortuno e non gioco al meglio, sarò pubblicamente gettato in pasto ai lupi'. Non credo che vi siate fatti un favore”. Il timore è che la gestione pubblica del caso Musiala possa compromettere la fiducia degli altri giocatori nei confronti della società, proprio mentre il Bayern cerca di consolidare il proprio progetto tecnico.

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 14:59 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 18 November 2026.

Bayern Munich's chief executive has confirmed Vincent Kompany is expected to return to the dugout on Friday, less than a month after collapsing at the club's training ground.

Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching Bayern's Under-23 side and reportedly suffered from seizures.

The 40-year-old, who suffered a dislocated shoulder in the fall, underwent tests in hospital which determined that a 'meningeal irritation' had been the cause of his collapse.

Sources indicate that if left untreated meningeal irritation can become meningitis. The meninges are the membranes around the brain and spinal cord.

Kompany was discharged from hospital the following week to continue his recovery at home.

The Belgian coach is now set to return to the dugout when Bayern face Cologne on Friday, with Kompany due to also address the media tomorrow morning.

Vincent Kompany is set to return to the Bayern Munich dugout for their Bundesliga match on Friday.

Kompany's return was officially confirmed by Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen.

According to recent reports, 'Yes, Vincent is in pretty good spirits. I ran into him today,' Dreesen told German outlet Abendzeitung.

Sources indicate that 'The meningeal irritation has healed. He has already undergone shoulder surgery.'.

Kompany had led training for the first time since his collapse earlier this week, with his arm reportedly in a sling following his shoulder injury.

He had missed five matches during his recovery with Bayern winning two and drawing against Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga.

The German champions also beat Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in his absence, as well as progressing in the DFB Cup.

Kompany's assistant Aaron Danks had overseen the first team during his recovery.

Danks previously worked as Kompany's assistant at Anderlecht before deputising for Dean Smith and Steven Gerrard at Aston Villa and Michael Carrick at Middlesbrough.

Kompany has missed five matches following his collapse at Bayern's training ground on October 23.

Bayern had stressed they wanted to give Kompany as much time as required to recover before returning to work.

The German giants play eight matches in the next month, including two matches in the Champions League, before the Bundesliga takes its winter break.

Reports had emerged after Kompany's collapse that club officials had been concerned by his irregular eating habits, as well as barely exercising, drinking excessive amounts of coffee, and taking on too much work.

Bayern sporting director Max Eberl dismissed the claims last month, reiterating that Kompany's illness had been the cause of his collapse rather than his workload.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a big game for United and Carrick.

In a recent development, “We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a significant game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win quickly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

In a recent development, gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

“We take it how it is. For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s latest home or at least they will when everything is in order.
